summary: The area's two roadmaps, Exchangeability and StandardDistributions, are mathematically sound. No layer statement is false except one Wishart congruence target (finding 19). The findings concern the atlas record and the libraries. Most layers are already built in Tau Ceti at f790474: Exchangeability layers 0–3 and 5–7, and StandardDistributions layers 0–4 and most of layer 5. The atlas still records every layer as 'unknown'. The accepted audit AUDIT-40, which covers both roadmaps, is still pending in data/library-coverage.json, and it needs corrections before it is merged. Exchangeability layer 4 lacks the Lᵖ reverse-martingale theorem, and the Gaussian-Gram Wishart characteristic function is not built; AUDIT-40 marks both complete. Two targets are under-planned. Aldous–Hoover (Exchangeability layer 8) is named without a statement or prerequisites, and the real-degree inverse-Wishart moments have no route. There are three duplications: dissociation and exchangeable relational laws with DenseGraphLimits 9b; the generic Koopman ergodic infrastructure with AdditiveCombinatorics AC.2; and the Gaussian covariance pushforward with OptimalTransport layer 5. The StandardDistributions stages also have no prerequisite edges, although the document states them.

findings.claim: Two roadmaps plan the dissociation, extremality and graph-case representation theory of exchangeable relational laws, and nothing connects them. DenseGraphLimits Layer 9b plans IsDissociated, the extremality theorem exists_graphon_of_isDissociated and the dissociated ⇔ Dirac characterisation for exchangeable graph laws. It calls these 'specializations, not a parallel theory', assigns the generic API to this roadmap and says the generic representation theorem 'owes a specialization/compatibility result'. This Layer 8 plans no generic relational-law API, no symmetric-irreflexive specialisation and no compatibility theorem. The library already shows the split: two unbridged dissociation predicates, one on ExchangeableGraphLaw (finite label windows) and one on ℕ × ℕ-indexed arrays (with an ergodicity characterisation). Diaconis–Janson note that the two representation theorems are interderivable, so without an owner the graph case is proved twice with no stated compatibility.

findings.claim: As stated, the full-row-rank congruence target for the nonsingular Wishart family is false. When q < p and q − 1 < n ≤ p − 1, the source nonsingularWishartMeasure n S is the zero measure, so its pushforward is zero, but the stated target nonsingularWishartMeasure n (M S Mᵀ) is a probability measure. The only justification the layer gives is 'Full row rank keeps the new scale matrix positive-definite'. It does not require the source degree hypothesis (p:ℝ) − 1 < n, or S.PosDef, and the principal-submatrix marginal it asks to record as a special case has the same defect. Counterexample: p = 2, q = 1, M = (1 0), S = 1, n = 1/2.
findings.evidence: Layer 6 item 4: 'For `M : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin p) ℝ` with `M.rank = q`, prove that the pushforward under `A ↦ M * A * Mᵀ` is `nonsingularWishartMeasure n (M * S * Mᵀ)`. Full row rank keeps the new scale matrix positive-definite. ... Record invertible congruence and principal-submatrix marginals as special cases.' The same item defines the family: 'When `S.PosDef` and `(p : ℝ) - 1 < n`, define the law ... Define this measure to be zero when either parameter hypothesis fails.' With p = 2 and n = 1/2 the source is 0, since 1 ≮ 1/2. The target has q = 1, and 0 < 1/2 with M S Mᵀ = (1) positive definite, so it is a probability law (a chi-squared law with 1/2 degree of freedom). The blanket convention at README line 91 ('Every probability theorem carries either the classical hypotheses or a listed boundary case') does not say whose hypotheses apply, and the target family's hypotheses do not suffice. No Tau Ceti declaration exists yet (no nonsingularWishart at f790474), so the statement is still to be written.

findings.claim: Item 6 asks for the inverse-Wishart mean (n − p − 1)⁻¹ • S when p + 1 < n, and for non-integrability of the identity when p − 1 < n ≤ p + 1, both for real degree n. No layer plans an input that yields these for non-integer n. Bartlett (item 5) is restricted to natural ν with p ≤ ν, the law of a Schur complement of a Wishart matrix is not planned, and neither are orthogonal invariance of E[A⁻¹] or an integration-by-parts identity on the cone. The planned transforms (trace mgf, charFun) give moments of A, not of A⁻¹, and the inverse-Wishart density alone does not make the mean routine. The natural route needs two things. First, the Cholesky factorization of nonsingularWishartMeasure n 1 for real n > p − 1: this is item 5's computation, which uses only the item 2 Jacobian and never the integrality of n. Second, the observation that 1/(A⁻¹)_{p−1,p−1} = L_{p−1,p−1}² has law chiSquaredMeasure (n − p + 1). Then E[1/χ²_k] = 1/(k − 2), which is finite iff k > 2, gives exactly the item 6 threshold n > p + 1.
findings.evidence: Layer 6 item 5: '**Bartlett decomposition.** Let `ν : ℕ` with `p ≤ ν`. Lift `nonsingularWishartMeasure (ν : ℝ) 1` ...'. Item 6: 'If `0 < p` and `(p : ℝ) + 1 < n`, prove mean `(n - (p : ℝ) - 1)⁻¹ • Sₛ`. Within the valid family, prove non-integrability of the identity at and below that threshold.' Here n is the real degree of 'nonsingularWishartMeasure n S⁻¹'. The Layer 6 text contains no Schur-complement Wishart law, no real-degree Bartlett and no orthogonal-invariance statement (searched README lines 685-898 for Schur, real degree, orthogonal, invariance). At f790474 no Bartlett, nonsingularWishart or inverseWishart declaration exists. Available inputs: TauCeti.map_cholesky_symmetricLebesgue (TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/SymmetricMatrix/Cholesky.lean:304), whose Jacobian density is degree-free; TauCeti.Probability.integral_id_inverseGammaMeasure (hr : 0 < r) (ha : 1 < a) giving r/(a−1) (TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/InverseGamma.lean:357); integrable_id_inverseGammaMeasure_iff giving 'Integrable id (inverseGammaMeasure a r) ↔ 1 < a' (:404); chiSquaredMeasure_eq_gammaMeasure (ChiSquared.lean:190). With a = (n−p+1)/2 and r = 1/2 these give mean 1/(n−p−1) exactly when n > p+1.
findings.fix: Add to the owner of Layer 6 items 5-6, as a maintainer note or as nodes in the Layer 6 blueprint packet: (a) a real-degree Cholesky factorization of nonsingularWishartMeasure n 1 for (p:ℝ) − 1 < n, with independent (L i i)² ~ chiSquaredMeasure (n − i) and L i j ~ gaussianReal 0 1 for j < i, of which item 5 is the natural-degree case; (b) invariance of nonsingularWishartMeasure n 1 under congruence by orthogonal matrices, a special case of item 4's invertible congruence, so that E[A⁻¹] is a scalar multiple of 1; (c) (A⁻¹)_{p−1,p−1} = 1/(L_{p−1,p−1})² for lower-triangular L.
